sanskrit: vimṛśya ca tato rāmo vayasyam akutobhayam pratardanaṃ kāśipatiṃ pariṣvajyedam abravīt
english: Then Rāma, having deliberated, embraced his fearless friend Pratardana, lord of Kāśī, and spoke these words.

sanskrit: darśitā bhavatā prītir darśitaṃ sauhṛdaṃ param udyogaś ca kṛto rājan bharatena tvayā saha
english: "Affection has been shown by you, supreme friendship has been shown, and great effort has been made, O king, by you together with Bharata."

sanskrit: tad bhavān adya kāśeyīṃ purīṃ vārāṇasīṃ vraja ramaṇīyāṃ tvayā guptāṃ suprākārāṃ sutoraṇām
english: "Therefore let Your Honour now go to Vārāṇasī, the city of the Kāśīs, that beautiful city protected by you, with its fine ramparts and splendid gateways."

sanskrit: etāvad uktvā utthāya kākutsthaḥ paramāsanāt paryaṣvajata dharmātmā nirantaram urogatam
english: Having said so much, the righteous-souled Kākutstha rose from his exalted seat and embraced that friend, pressing him close to his chest.

sanskrit: visṛjya taṃ vayasyaṃ sa svāgatān pṛthivīpatīn prahasan rāghavo vākyam uvāca madhurākṣaram
english: Having dismissed that companion, Rāghava, smiling, addressed the kings who had come as guests with words of sweet syllables.

sanskrit: bhavatāṃ prītir avyagrā tejasā parirakṣitā dharmaś ca niyato nityaṃ satyaṃ ca bhavatāṃ sadā
english: "Your unwavering affection has been guarded by your valour; dharma has ever been constant for you, and so has truth, always."

sanskrit: yuṣmākaṃ ca prabhāvena tejasā ca mahātmanām hato durātmā durbuddhī rāvaṇo rākṣasādhipaḥ
english: "Through your might and through the valour of your great selves, Rāvaṇa the wicked-souled, evil-minded lord of rākṣasas has been slain."

sanskrit: hetumātram ahaṃ tatra bhavatāṃ tejasāṃ hataḥ rāvaṇaḥ sagaṇo yuddhe saputraḥ sahabāndhavaḥ
english: "I was merely the instrument there; by your collective splendour, Rāvaṇa with his horde in battle, with his sons and all his kinsmen, was destroyed."

sanskrit: bhavantaś ca samānītā bharatena mahātmanā śrutvā janakarājasya kānane tanayāṃ hṛtām
english: "And you were all assembled by the great-souled Bharata upon hearing that the daughter of the king of Janaka had been abducted in the forest."

sanskrit: udyuktānāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ pārthivānāṃ mahātmanām kālo hy atītaḥ sumahān gamane rocatāṃ matiḥ
english: "A very long time has passed for all the striving great-souled kings in this undertaking; let your minds be inclined toward departure."

sanskrit: pratyūcus taṃ ca rājāno harṣeṇa mahatānvitāḥ diṣṭyā tvaṃ vijayī rāma rājyaṃ cāpi pratiṣṭhitam
english: The kings, filled with great joy, replied to him: "By good fortune you are victorious, Rāma, and your kingdom too is firmly established."

sanskrit: diṣṭyā pratyāhṛtā sītā diṣṭyā śatruḥ parājitaḥ eṣa naḥ paramaḥ kāma eṣā naḥ kīrtir uttamā
english: "By good fortune Sītā has been recovered; by good fortune the enemy has been defeated. This is our highest desire; this is our supreme glory."

sanskrit: yat tvāṃ vijayinaṃ rāma paśyāmo hataśātravam upapannaṃ ca kākutstha yat tvam asmān praśaṃsasi
english: "That we behold you victorious, Rāma, your enemies slain — and it is fitting, O Kākutstha, that you should praise us."

sanskrit: praśaṃsārhā hi jānanti praśaṃsāṃ vaktum īdṛśīm āpṛcchāmo gamiṣyāmo hṛdistho naḥ sadā bhavān
english: "For those worthy of praise know how to speak such praise. We take our leave; we shall depart. You dwell in our hearts always."

sanskrit: bhavec ca te mahārāja prītir asmāsu nityadā
english: "And may your affection for us, O great king, endure eternally."

sanskrit: te prayātā mahātmānaḥ pārthivāḥ sarvato diśam kampayanto mahīṃ vīrāḥ svapurāṇi prahṛṣṭavat
english: Those great-souled kings, those heroes, departed in all directions, making the earth tremble, heading joyfully to their own cities.

sanskrit: akṣauhiṇī sahasrais te samavetās tv anekaśaḥ hṛṣṭāḥ pratigatāḥ sarve rāghavārthe samāgatāḥ
english: Gathered with thousands of akṣauhiṇī armies in manifold ways, all those who had assembled for Rāghava's sake returned home, rejoicing.

sanskrit: ūcuś caiva mahīpālā baladarpasamanvitāḥ na nāma rāvaṇaṃ yuddhe paśyāmaḥ purataḥ sthitam
english: And the rulers of the earth, proud of their strength, declared: "We never even got to see Rāvaṇa standing before us in battle!"

sanskrit: bharatena vayaṃ paścāt samānītā nirarthakam hatā hi rākṣasās tatra pārthivaiḥ syur na saṃśayaḥ
english: "We were assembled afterwards by Bharata to no purpose at all — the rākṣasas there would surely have been slain by the kings, of that there is no doubt."

sanskrit: rāmasya bāhuvīryeṇa pālitā lakṣmaṇasya ca sukhaṃ pāre samudrasya yudhyema vigatajvarāḥ
english: "Protected by the arm-strength of Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, we could have fought with ease on the far shore of the ocean, free from anxiety."

sanskrit: etāś cānyāś ca rājānaḥ kathās tatra sahasraśaḥ kathayantaḥ svarāṣṭrāṇi viviśus te mahārathāḥ
english: Speaking these and thousands of other such stories, those great chariot-warriors entered their respective kingdoms.

sanskrit: yathāpurāṇi te gatvā ratnāni vividhāni ca rāmāya priyakāmārtham upahārān nṛpā daduḥ
english: Arriving at their own cities, those kings, desiring to please Rāma, presented various gems as offerings to him.

sanskrit: aśvān ratnāni vastrāṇi hastinaś ca madotkaṭān candanāni ca divyāni divyāny ābharaṇāni ca
english: Horses, gems, garments, elephants overflowing with rut, divine sandalwood, and divine ornaments.

sanskrit: bharato lakṣmaṇaś caiva śatrughnaś ca mahārathaḥ ādāya tāni ratnāni ayodhyām agaman punaḥ
english: Bharata, Lakṣmaṇa, and the great chariot-warrior Śatrughna took those gems and returned again to Ayodhyā.

sanskrit: āgatāś ca purīṃ ramyām ayodhyāṃ puruṣarṣabhāḥ daduḥ sarvāṇi ratnāni rāghavāya mahātmane
english: Having arrived at the beautiful city of Ayodhyā, those bulls among men presented all the gems to the great-souled Rāghava.

sanskrit: pratigṛhya ca tat sarvaṃ prītiyuktaḥ sa rāghavaḥ sarvāṇi tāni pradadau sugrīvāya mahātmane
english: Receiving all that with joy, Rāghava distributed all of it to the great-souled Sugrīva.

sanskrit: vibhīṣaṇāya ca dadau ye cānye ṛkṣavānarāḥ hanūmatpramukhā vīrā rākṣasāś ca mahābalāḥ
english: He gave also to Vibhīṣaṇa, and to those other bears and vānaras headed by Hanūmat — those heroes — and to the mighty rākṣasas.

sanskrit: te sarve hṛṣṭamanaso rāmadattāni tāny atha śirobhir dhārayām āsur bāhubhiś ca mahābalāḥ
english: All of them, joyful of heart, then bore those gifts given by Rāma upon their heads and in their arms, those of great strength.

sanskrit: papuś caiva sugandhīni madhūni vividhāni ca māṃsāni ca sumṛṣṭāni phalāny āsvādayanti ca
english: They drank fragrant mead of various kinds, and savoured well-prepared meats and fruits.

sanskrit: evaṃ teṣāṃ nivasatāṃ māsaḥ sāgro gatas tadā muhūrtam iva tat sarvaṃ rāmabhaktyā samarthayan
english: As they resided thus, more than a month passed — all of it seemed but a moment, sustained as they were by devotion to Rāma.

sanskrit: reme rāmaḥ sa taiḥ sārdhaṃ vānaraiḥ kāmarūpibhiḥ rājabhiś ca mahāvīryai rākṣasaiś ca mahābalaiḥ
english: Rāma took pleasure with those vānaras of wish-assuming form, with those kings of great valour, and with those mighty rākṣasas.

sanskrit: evaṃ teṣāṃ yayau māso dvitīyaḥ śaiśiraḥ sukham vānarāṇāṃ prahṛṣṭānāṃ rākṣasānāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ
english: Thus a second winter month passed happily for all those rejoicing vānaras and rākṣasas alike.

sanskrit: tathā sma teṣāṃ vasatām ṛkṣavānararakṣasām rāghavas tu mahātejāḥ sugrīvam idam abravīt
english: As those bears, vānaras, and rākṣasas were dwelling there in that manner, the great-resplendent Rāghava said this to Sugrīva:

sanskrit: gamyatāṃ saumya kiṣkindhāṃ durādharṣaṃ surāsuraiḥ pālayasva sahāmātyai rājyaṃ nihatakaṇṭakam
english: "Go, dear friend, to Kiṣkindhā, impregnable to gods and asuras. Rule your kingdom together with your ministers, now that its thorns have been removed."

sanskrit: aṅgadaṃ ca mahābāho prītyā paramayānvitaḥ paśya tvaṃ hanumantaṃ ca nalaṃ ca sumahābalam
english: "And, O mighty-armed one, look with the greatest affection upon Aṅgada, upon Hanūmat, and upon the supremely powerful Nala."

sanskrit: suṣeṇaṃ śvaśuraṃ śūraṃ tāraṃ ca balināṃ varam kumudaṃ caiva durdharṣaṃ nīlaṃ ca sumahābalam
english: "Upon Suṣeṇa your heroic father-in-law, upon Tāra the best among the strong, upon the irresistible Kumuda, and upon the supremely powerful Nīla."

sanskrit: vīraṃ śatabaliṃ caiva maindaṃ dvividam eva ca gajaṃ gavākṣaṃ gavayaṃ śarabhaṃ ca mahābalam
english: "Upon the heroic Śatabali, upon Mainda and Dvivida, upon Gaja, Gavākṣa, Gavaya, and the mighty Śarabha."

sanskrit: ṛkṣarājaṃ ca durdharṣaṃ jāmbavantaṃ mahābalam paśya prītisamāyukto gandhamādanam eva ca
english: "Look with affection upon the irresistible king of bears, the mighty Jāmbavān, and upon Gandhamādana as well."

sanskrit: ye cānye sumahātmāno madarthe tyaktajīvitāḥ paśya tvaṃ prītisaṃyukto mā caiṣāṃ vipriyaṃ kṛthāḥ
english: "And those other great souls who laid down their lives for my sake — look upon them with affection, and do nothing that would displease them."

sanskrit: evam uktvā ca sugrīvaṃ praśasya ca punaḥ punaḥ vibhīṣaṇam athovāca rāmo madhurayā girā
english: Having spoken thus and having praised Sugrīva again and again, Rāma then addressed Vibhīṣaṇa with sweet speech:

sanskrit: taṅkāṃ praśādhi dharmeṇa saṃmato hy asi pārthiva purasya rākṣasānāṃ ca bhrātur vaiśvaraṇasya ca
english: "Rule Laṅkā righteously — for you are the acknowledged king, O lord of the earth, of the city of the rākṣasas, equal to your brother Vaiśravaṇa."

sanskrit: mā ca buddhim adharme tvaṃ kuryā rājan kathaṃ cana buddhimanto hi rājāno dhruvam aśnanti medinīm
english: "And never, O king, under any circumstance, turn your mind to unrighteousness. For the wise among kings do surely inherit the earth."

sanskrit: ahaṃ ca nityaśo rājan sugrīvasahitas tvayā smartavyaḥ parayā prītyā gaccha tvaṃ vigatajvaraḥ
english: "And, O king, remember me always together with Sugrīva, with the highest affection. Go now, free from anxiety."

sanskrit: rāmasya bhāṣitaṃ śrutvā ṛṣkavānararākṣasāḥ sādhu sādhv iti kākutsthaṃ praśaśaṃsuḥ punaḥ punaḥ
english: Hearing the words of Rāma, the bears, vānaras, and rākṣasas praised Kākutstha saying "Well done! Well done!" again and again.

sanskrit: tava buddhir mahābāho vīryam adbhutam eva ca mādhuryaṃ paramaṃ rāma svayambhor iva nityadā
english: "Your wisdom, O mighty-armed one, your wondrous valour, and your supreme sweetness of nature, Rāma, are ever like those of the Self-born Brahmā."

sanskrit: teṣām evaṃ bruvāṇānāṃ vānarāṇāṃ ca rakṣasām hanūmatpraṇato bhūtvā rāghavaṃ vākyam abravīt
english: While the vānaras and rākṣasas were speaking thus, Hanūmat bowed down and addressed Rāghava with these words:

sanskrit: sneho me paramo rājaṃs tvayi nityaṃ pratiṣṭhitaḥ bhaktiś ca niyatā vīra bhāvo nānyatra gacchati
english: "My highest love, O king, is permanently established in you; my devotion is constant, O hero — my heart goes nowhere else."

sanskrit: yāvad rāmakathāṃ vīra śroṣye 'haṃ pṛthivītale tāvac charīre vatsyantu mama prāṇā na saṃśayaḥ
english: "As long as I shall hear the story of Rāma upon this earth, O hero, so long shall my life-breaths dwell within my body — of this there is no doubt."

sanskrit: evaṃ bruvāṇaṃ rājendro hanūmantam athāsanāt utthāya ca pariṣvajya vākyam etad uvāca ha
english: Hearing Hanūmat speak thus, the lord of kings rose from his seat, embraced him, and then spoke these words:

sanskrit: evam etat kapiśreṣṭha bhavitā nātra saṃśayaḥ lokā hi yāvat sthāsyanti tāvat sthāsyati me kathā
english: "So shall it be, O best of monkeys — of this there is no doubt. As long as the worlds shall endure, so long shall my story endure."

sanskrit: cariṣyati kathā yāval lokān eṣā hi māmikā tāvac charīre vatsyanti prāṇās tava na saṃśayaḥ
english: "As long as this story of mine shall travel through the worlds, so long shall your life-breaths dwell in your body — of this there is no doubt."

sanskrit: tato 'sya hāraṃ candrābhaṃ mucya kaṇṭhāt sa rāghavaḥ vaidūryataralaṃ snehād ābabandhe hanūmati
english: Then Rāghava removed from his own neck a garland bright as the moon, trembling with vaidūrya gems, and fastened it with affection upon Hanūmat.

sanskrit: tenorasi nibaddhena hāreṇa sa mahākapiḥ rarāja hemaśailendraś candreṇākrāntamastakaḥ
english: With that garland bound upon his chest, that great monkey shone like the lord of golden mountains with the moon crowning his summit.

sanskrit: śrutvā tu rāghavasyaitad utthāyotthāya vānarāḥ praṇamya śirasā pādau prajagmus te mahābalāḥ
english: Hearing this from Rāghava, the vānaras rose up one after another, bowed their heads to his feet, and those mighty ones departed.

sanskrit: sugrīvaś caiva rāmeṇa pariṣvakto mahābhujaḥ vibhīṣaṇaś ca dharmātmā nirantaram urogataḥ
english: The mighty-armed Sugrīva was embraced by Rāma, and the righteous-souled Vibhīṣaṇa was held close to his chest.

sanskrit: sarve ca te bāṣpagalāḥ sāśrunetrā vicetasaḥ saṃmūḍhā iva duḥkhena tyajante rāghavaṃ tadā
english: And all of them, their voices choked with tears, their eyes filled with tears, bewildered, as if stupefied by grief, departed from Rāghava then.
